My dear [Miss Jacob](/person/749),
We were so sorry to have missed you. I meant to have written that same evening but somehow missed doing so.

If you can give us another chance, the best time would be earlier in the day - as my [mother](/person/1606) now does not leave her room till 2 or 3 o’clock so that if you could drive over in the forenoon, and stay to luncheon, we should be more sure of seeing you.

Alice will I hope be here till near the middle of the month, but the sooner you can be kind enough to drive over the better[^1]

yours sincerely

C M Yonge


[^1]: [Alice Moberly](/person/1025) was a contemporary of Edith Jacob\'s, and she, rather than [Alice Coleridge](/person/327), is probably referred to here.
